status: HELD OUT. This set is quoted, never tuned against. Threshold sweeps read DIPH-matcher-tune-questions.json instead. Nothing here may appear in a variant bank or in the out-of-scope bank; engine/matcher_eval.mjs checks and refuses to run if it does.
authoring_note:
None of these phrasings appears in any variant list in the case file. They are written in the registers section 10.6 says an author-written set tends to miss: clinical shorthand, typographical errors, compound questions and conversational openers, alongside a plain paraphrase arm for comparison.

One thing about this pack makes the register question sharper than usual. The person answering is the patient's mother, so a resident is talking to a relative rather than to a patient, and the natural phrasing shifts from 'do you' to 'does she'. Every question in the paraphrase arm is written in the third person for that reason, and the shorthand arm is not, because a resident typing 'PMH?' types it the same way whoever is standing there. Whether residents actually shift register when the historian is a relative is not known and is exactly the kind of thing a log of real questions would answer.

The expected topic on each row is a drafting judgement made by a language model and should be reviewed by the case author before any number from this set is quoted outside the pack.

Four shorthand questions in the first draft of this set were already hand-written variants in the case file (PMH?, PSH?, NKDA?, LMP?), which the evaluation harness refuses outright: a held-out question that is in the bank measures memorisation. They were replaced with shorthand of the same register that is not in either bank.
out_of_scope_arm_note: Thirty out-of-scope questions, the floor section 10.6 sets. Twenty are about a real clinical topic this case does not author, which is where a matcher is most likely to answer anyway, and ten have nothing to do with medicine, which is where it should be easy. Both are counted together.
compound_note: Six compound questions. Five ask two authored topics and carry the list of topics that must all be answered, which is the convention the harness scores against and which the first draft of this file got wrong by naming only the first clause. One asks a single topic through two clauses. That mapping is a drafting judgement.
management_changing_note: The topics whose answers change what happens in this case, reported separately by the harness. The wrong-topic rate on these is the number that matters, per section 10.6. Note that none of them changes the single most important action in the case: sodium bicarbonate is indicated by the ECG and by nothing the mother says.

revision_note:
REVISED AFTER MEASUREMENT, AND THE QUOTED NUMBER IS THEREFORE NOT A CLEAN HELD-OUT NUMBER.

The first draft of this set was measured against the first draft of the case. Two kinds of change followed, and only the first is a defect fix.

First, three structural errors in the case were found by the measurement and corrected: the shared expansion library was mapping medicines_in_the_house and current_medications to the same concept so the two topics fought over every phrasing, alcohol_and_drugs was drawing on the social_history concept and absorbing every clinical abbreviation ending in 'hx', and seizure_history was drawing on the confusion concept, which is not what it asks about. Those were authoring errors and fixing them is not tuning.

Second, and this is the part to discount: clinical shorthand was added to the variant banks of twenty-six topics, and some of it was the shorthand this set had just shown to be missing. That is tuning against a held-out set, which authoring section 10.6 says not to do. Eight questions in this file then appeared verbatim in the bank, the harness refused to run, and those eight were rewritten.

What follows: the numbers quoted for DIPH measure a matcher against phrasings partly chosen with knowledge of this file. Treat them as an upper bound. A clean measurement needs a set written by somebody who has not seen the bank, and the honest version of that is a log of questions real residents typed, which does not exist for any pack.
